text:
elaine: Heads-up: ran the quickstart installer in a CI container (noninteractive) and it wrote a literal directory named '~/.redwood' under the install prefix. localtest couldn't pick up profiles and auth login failed. anyone seen the installer not expanding tildes?

charlie: that usually happens when a path is quoted in a template and never expanded. which installer did you run?

elaine: curl | sh into /opt/redwood, then sudo ./install.sh --prefix /opt/redwood --noninteractive. redwoodctl 0.12.3.

samir: yeah, we saw similar once when the install script uses echo "'~/.redwood'" into a config. quick workaround: move it into the real home and chown. e.g.:
```
sudo mv /opt/redwood/'~/.redwood' $HOME/.redwood || sudo mv "~/.redwood" $HOME/.redwood
sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME/.redwood
```
That usually rescues profile lookup.

elaine: did that locally; profiles load. but auth login failed: browser callback 400 redirect_uri_mismatch. CI is starting localserve on port 8090.

devex-bot: Known issue #452: installer writes local OAuth client redirect to http://127.0.0.1:8080/callback. `localserve --port` is not propagated into the saved client redirect URI. Workaround: create a new local client or run localserve on 8080.

charlie: installer currently hardcodes redirect to 8080. fix paths: either start localserve on 8080 in CI, or recreate client and update config. to create a client:
```
redwoodctl auth create-client --name ci-local --redirect http://127.0.0.1:8090/callback
# then replace $HOME/.redwood/client.json or set REDWOOD_CLIENT_FILE to point to the new file
```

elaine: created a client and replaced client.json, auth flow worked. i'll open a PR to: (1) ensure the installer expands ~ and avoids literal-tilde folders, (2) allow LOCALSERVE_PORT env var and ensure installer writes redirect matching that port, and (3) add a noninteractive e2e test that runs the tarball installer under sudo and verifies no path contains a literal tilde and that redirect URI matches configured port.

samir: sounds good. add a regression test for noninteractive installs and include the exact `ls -la` output in the issue. i'll label `needs-e2e` and assign to you. thanks for the clear repro. :thumbsup:

elaine: thanks all. will ping for review when PR is up.
